$comment: One entry per (checkov check id, resource) the Terraform side fails and the
CloudFormation side does not: `resource` is `<nested-stack path>/<LogicalId>` for a
translated resource, or the bare Terraform address of one the translator adds.
An entry matching no finding fails the gate, and so does a change in
notEvaluatedCount: Terraform findings on conditional resources checkov skips on the
CloudFormation side because their condition is false at the parameter defaults.

entries.reason: the custom-resource bridge (terraform/translator/idp_tf/static_files.py bridge_tf), which the translator adds to every module with custom resources; CloudFormation runs custom resources inside the service and has no resource to compare it with. No reserved concurrency: Terraform invokes it one custom resource at a time per apply, and the template's own custom-resource handlers skip the same check for the same reason (they scale on demand).

the custom-resource bridge (terraform/translator/idp_tf/static_files.py bridge_tf), which the translator adds to every module with custom resources; CloudFormation runs custom resources inside the service and has no resource to compare it with. A dead-letter queue applies to asynchronous invocations only; Terraform's aws_lambda_invocation calls the bridge synchronously and a failure fails the apply, so there is nothing for a DLQ to catch.

the custom-resource bridge (terraform/translator/idp_tf/static_files.py bridge_tf), which the translator adds to every module with custom resources; CloudFormation runs custom resources inside the service and has no resource to compare it with. Not in a VPC: it calls only AWS APIs (Lambda and S3), as the template's custom-resource handlers that skip the same check do.

the custom-resource bridge (terraform/translator/idp_tf/static_files.py bridge_tf), which the translator adds to every module with custom resources; CloudFormation runs custom resources inside the service and has no resource to compare it with. Its one environment variable is the name of its own bucket, which is not secret; the default Lambda-managed key encrypts it at rest.

the custom-resource bridge (terraform/translator/idp_tf/static_files.py bridge_tf), which the translator adds to every module with custom resources; CloudFormation runs custom resources inside the service and has no resource to compare it with. Known gap, not a decision: the template encrypts its functions' log groups with the deployment's customer-managed key and the bridge's log group uses CloudWatch's default encryption. The bridge logs the request type and logical id of each custom resource, not its properties. Remove this entry when bridge_tf takes the key.

the custom-resource bridge (terraform/translator/idp_tf/static_files.py bridge_tf), which the translator adds to every module with custom resources; CloudFormation runs custom resources inside the service and has no resource to compare it with. No access logging: the bucket holds the bridge's transient response objects, physical ids, the label template and the resource directory, all written and read by the deployment's own roles; This is a gap relative to the template's data buckets, which log to the logging bucket.

the custom-resource bridge (terraform/translator/idp_tf/static_files.py bridge_tf), which the translator adds to every module with custom resources; CloudFormation runs custom resources inside the service and has no resource to compare it with. No versioning: every object in it is regenerated by an apply (the label template, the resource directory) or is a single custom-resource response consumed once; a lifecycle rule expires the responses.
